metadata.governance_rule: Resolutions without verified reviewer authorization are strictly prohibited.

case_a.title: K. Bhaskaran v. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan (High Court Reference Interpretation)
case_a.proposition: Territorial jurisdiction under Section 138 NI Act can be initiated at any of the five places where statutory acts were performed, including place of issue of notice.

case_b.title: Harman Electronics Pvt Ltd v. National Panasonic India Pvt Ltd
case_b.proposition: Issuance of statutory notice alone from a particular territory does not confer jurisdiction to initiate proceedings under Section 138 NI Act.

conflicts.priority_rationale: National commercial uniformity in cheque dishonour prosecutions across financial capitals.
conflicts.reviewer_decision_rationale: Resolved definitively by Supreme Court in Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod (2014) 9 SCC 129, and subsequent Parliament statutory amendment inserting Section 142(2) in 2015.

case_a.title: Union of India v. State of Maharashtra (BHC Interlocutory Analysis)
case_a.proposition: Bar under Section 18 of SC/ST Act against anticipatory bail is absolute once prima facie allegations are made in FIR.

case_b.title: Virendra Singh v. State of Rajasthan
case_b.proposition: Pre-arrest bail can be granted notwithstanding Section 18 if allegations on face of record are patently false and motivated.

conflicts.governing_statute_section: Section 18 & 18A, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989
conflicts.priority_rationale: Fundamental personal liberty under Article 21 balanced against statutory protection for vulnerable communities.
conflicts.reviewer_decision_rationale: Supreme Court in Prathvi Raj Chauhan v. Union of India (2020) 4 SCC 727 clarified that pre-arrest bail is maintainable only if no prima facie case is made out.

case_a.title: National Highways Authority of India v. Bhubaneswar Expressway
case_a.proposition: Court can entertain Section 9 petition post-constitution of arbitral tribunal only if petitioner proves remedy under Section 17 is inefficacious.

case_b.title: Dirk India Pvt Ltd v. Maharashtra State Electricity Transmission Co
case_b.proposition: Section 9 remedy remains concurrently available post-award only for successful party to protect fruits of award.

conflicts.priority_rationale: Divergent commercial arbitration enforcement practices across infrastructure contractors in Delhi and Mumbai.
conflicts.reviewer_decision_rationale: Currently under advocate triage to delineate pre-award vs post-award scope under 2015 Arbitration Amendment.

case_a.title: Rajiv Chakraborty Resolution Professional v. Directorate of Enforcement
case_a.proposition: Section 14 IBC moratorium does not interdict criminal attachment proceedings under Section 5 of Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

case_b.title: Directorate of Enforcement v. Manoj Kumar Agarwal
case_b.proposition: IBC Section 238 non-obstante clause overrides PMLA attachment once Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process has commenced.

conflicts.priority_rationale: Critical conflict between resolution of corporate debt and proceeds of crime confiscation affecting thousands of insolvency proceedings.
conflicts.reviewer_decision_rationale: Confirmed genuine conflict between Delhi High Court writ interpretation and NCLAT statutory precedence; pending resolution before Supreme Court three-judge bench.

case_a.title: Sunita Devi v. Ramesh Kumar
case_a.proposition: Maintenance awarded under Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act must be strictly adjusted against maintenance claimed under Section 125 CrPC.

case_b.title: Kavita Bai v. Suresh Singh
case_b.proposition: Section 125 CrPC is an independent social justice remedy and cannot be mechanically denied merely because nominal interim maintenance was granted in divorce proceeding.

conflicts.governing_statute_section: Section 125 CrPC 1973 vs Section 24 Hindu Marriage Act 1955
conflicts.priority_rationale: Family law maintenance overlap; factual quantum adequacy distinguishes individual orders.
conflicts.reviewer_decision_rationale: Supreme Court in Rajnesh v. Neha (2021) 2 SCC 324 formulated national uniform guidelines governing overlapping maintenance claims, requiring comprehensive disclosure affidavits.

case_a.title: D.Y. Beathel Enterprises v. State Tax Officer
case_a.proposition: Revenue must first exhaust recovery proceedings against defaulting supplier before reversing input tax credit from bona fide purchasing dealer under Section 16(2)(c) CGST Act.

case_b.title: Aastha Enterprises v. State of Bihar
case_b.proposition: Payment of tax by supplier into government treasury is mandatory condition precedent under Section 16(2)(c); purchaser cannot claim ITC if supplier defaulted, irrespective of bona fides.

conflicts.governing_statute_section: Section 16(2)(c), Central Goods and Services Tax Act 2017
conflicts.priority_rationale: Direct contradiction on taxpayer liability across states under nationwide GST statutory framework.
